FarguesFontaineDiamonds.title: Foundations of adic spaces, Part II: the Fargues-Fontaine curve as a diamond
FarguesFontaineDiamonds.reason: Start from unchanged AdicSpaces Layer 6, which owns the fixed E = Q_p adic curve over a characteristic-p perfectoid field. Add its marked-untilt functor of points, Frobenius-equivariant diamond quotient, site comparison, analytic untilt divisor and separately gated coefficient comparison. This early fixed-field branch is not reconstructed from relative bundle theory.

RelativeFarguesFontaine.title: Foundations of adic spaces, Part II: relative Fargues-Fontaine curves and period geometry
RelativeFarguesFontaine.reason: Extend the unchanged fixed-field adic construction to arbitrary perfectoid bases and all the stated local coefficient fields, importing the fixed-field diamond comparisons from FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0-F4, not its late F5. The genuinely new integral special fibre, relative annuli, degree-d divisors, line bundles and linear/G-torsor patching cannot be retired or merged into the fixed-field diamondification.

FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F0.keeps: The analytic/Z_p/Q_p and plus-ring interfaces needed to apply D6 to the existing fixed-field Y and X, and explicit transport under the permitted field, pseudouniformizer and chart choices. Import, rather than rebuild, W(F^+), its (p,[varpi])-adic topology and complete Huber pair, Y = D(p) intersect D([varpi]), its rational annuli and the adic Frobenius quotient. Retain the non-algebraically-closed field examples and the test excluding the union of the two opens.
FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F0.reason: The anchor already plans this complete fixed-field adic construction; it does not plan diamondification. Preserve its actual topology and plus rings, not just its set of points.

FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F1.reason: Keep the independent fixed-field comparison Y^diamond = S x Spd(Q_p) on all perfectoid test objects: actual marked untilts, the bounded continuous Witt/theta map, plus rings, naturality and gluing. This is not the integral product retaining V(p), and it does not assume the completed relative construction.

FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F2.keeps: The equivariance identity for the chosen Frobenius generator under F1, the diamond orbit relation coproduct_Z Y^diamond = Y^diamond x_(X^diamond) Y^diamond, the v-cover and effective quotient identification over Spd(Q_p), and the exact locality and choice-independence statements. Import the fixed adic windows, kappa scaling, properly discontinuous action and adic quotient/sheaf construction from the anchor. Do not claim that diamondification preserves arbitrary colimits or that X has a structural map to S.
FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F2.reason: The adic quotient is the immutable anchor theorem. The effective diamond relation and its marked generator are new comparison results, not duplicate quotient construction.

FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F3.keeps: Instantiate D6 on these actual Y and X, identify the resulting affinoid/etale sites and the Frobenius descent cocycle, and prove compatibility with the quotient and all allowed changes of charts. Import the general diamondification/site theorem. This uncoefficiented comparison completes the early geometric branch; ordinary invariants are not identified with derived invariants.
FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F3.reason: D6 owns the general analytic-adic/diamond etale-site equivalence; F3 owns its Frobenius-compatible Fargues-Fontaine instance.

FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F4.keeps: For the fixed E = Q_p curve, construct the analytic closed Cartier divisor from a marked untilt and descend it through the Frobenius quotient. Prove the actual annulus norm estimate, injectivity, closed image and complete-quotient/exact-sheaf statement, with its root-extension, tilt, Shilov-boundary and split topological-module descent steps. Import P1 only for the p-typical marked-untilt/primitive-ideal carrier and algebraic correspondence. Keep the distinction between a marked untilt, its Frobenius orbit, a divisor of a fixed curve and the Div^1 moduli sheaf. Export only the fixed-field analytic estimate as a seed for the relative proof, not a theorem for arbitrary bases or ramified E.
FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F4.reason: The primitive-ideal correspondence is not a second perfectoid carrier. The analytic closed-image theorem is substantial additional work and remains here. The independently reviewed limited F4-to-relative handoff is preserved.

FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F5.reason: Keep the late coefficient comparison after DiamondEtaleCohomology C2 and AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L0, with the specified ordinary/left-completed categories and finite-coefficient/derived-completion order. Retain RΓ, tensor and pullback comparisons. It is not an input to RF0-RF4 and does not supply unrestricted lower-shriek operations, properness or cohomological smoothness.

RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0.keeps: The ramified Witt/strict-lift construction for every stated E with residue F_q and every perfect coefficient algebra, including flatness, pi-adic completeness, Teichmuller lifts, q-Frobenius, functoriality, the equal-characteristic R[[pi]] model and all topology/uniformizer comparisons. Import the anchor fixed E = Q_p, perfectoid-field specialization and prove compatibility on actual rings. Keep the raw ramified-witt-universal-property proof prefix before the integral-Y/annuli children; RF0 as an aggregate is complete only after those children. Mathlib WittVector.lift is an inverse-limit map and does not discharge this strict-lift theorem.
RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0.reason: General coefficients and non-field bases remain genuinely new. The fixed-field case is a compatibility test against an existing owner, not permission to reconstruct it or assume ramified/equal-characteristic strict-lift theory.

RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y.reason: Keep the full relative integral construction curly-Y = Spa(W_OE(R^+)) minus V([varpi]) with its (pi,[varpi])-adic topology, rational charts, completed coordinate and plus rings, root-extension perfectoid/tilt comparison, split topological-module descent, gluing and integral product curly-Y^diamond = S x Spd(O_E). V(pi) is retained. The fixed-field generic restriction compares to F0/F1; those suppliers do not construct the special fibre. The raw RF0 strict-lift prefix is used before RF0 aggregate completion. At declaration level the coefficient input is the existing node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property, not the completed RF0 stage; do not insert an RF0 aggregate-to-child prerequisite. In the n = 1 root-extension chart of FS II.1.1 the tilt coordinate satisfies t_1^sharp = pi/[varpi], not [varpi]/pi. The chart keeps pi = 0 and inverts [varpi], so this coordinate is defined on the special fibre. Correct the reciprocal in the inherited chart-cover-perfectoidness-and-sheafiness proof step when reconciling that node; its identity and other targets are retained.

RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli.keeps: The generic restriction Y = curly-Y minus V(pi), relative radius windows and their completed coordinate/plus rings, restriction maps, base change, choice independence, relative sheafiness and the stated Stein/exhaustion and higher-acyclicity proof obligations. Import the anchor fixed-field annuli and their strong-noetherian theorem only for that specialization; compare the actual relative rings with them. The general non-noetherian relative proof still uses the stated stable-uniform/sousperfectoid and split-extension arguments, not a strong-noetherian claim for every base.
RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli.reason: The fixed-field annulus construction is duplicated only in the specialization. Relative topology, sheafiness, coordinate comparisons and their hypotheses must not disappear.

RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF1.keeps: Gluing of the relative generic Y and X, the chosen q-Frobenius action, its actual rational windows and quotient structure sheaves, base change for arbitrary perfectoid T to S, and the relative diamond presentation with its valuation, topology, plus-ring and cocycle compatibilities. RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF1.reason: The fixed-field diamond comparison and general site theorem each have an existing owner. The parameterized curve, sheaves and base-change theorem remain here.

RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2.reason: Keep this aggregate completion of integral-divisors and untilts, with both inputs and every original consumer. Do not treat the aggregate as an early constructor needed to establish its own children.

RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:integral-div.reason: Keep the full all-degree integral-divisor theory, including its necessary early relative degree-one closed-Cartier lemma, ordered primitive equations, descent of the unordered invertible ideal, the degree criterion, collisions, affineness locally on S where required, v-descent of vector bundles on divisors and thickenings, and ideal-adic completed/punctured rings with inverse-limit and generator-independence comparisons. The all-E/all-base version of the II.1.4 norm/closed-image argument is owned here before ordered products; the fixed Q_p-field analytic seed is imported from F4, and the relative/ramified descent remains to be proved. Reconcile the existing refined closed-cartier-divisor-norm-estimate node to this early ownership without deleting its proof or tests. The integral characteristic-p specialization is not renamed a characteristic-zero B_dR ring. The X_S branch requires RF1: its Cartier-divisor realization and local affineness pass through the actual relative Frobenius quotient (FS VI.1.2), not only through the fixed-field F2 specialization. Separate the collision test from the ordered-leg descent test: a specified double divisor 2D already has the ordered presentation (D,D), with equation xi^2 and multiplicity two. A splitting obstruction must instead be witnessed by suitable unsplit unordered leg data. Do not require a nontrivial splitting cover for every specified doubled leg; retain the general v-sheafification and descent obligations.

RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts.keeps: Marked generic E-untilts, their theta/primitive presentation with the exact ramified or equal-characteristic hypotheses, their degree-one divisors on Y and X and their Frobenius-orbit/naturality comparisons. Import P1 for the p-typical perfectoid correspondence; prove the additional E-linear comparison rather than assume it. Import the integral-divisors owner for the preceding all-base analytic closed-Cartier lemma and all-degree ideal completion/localization, then prove the generic d = 1 B_dR^+/B_dR, residue, filtration and graded-line comparisons, including the geometric DVR specialization. Retain divisor addition, disjointness/collision compatibility and source-qualified Div^1 properness/smoothness obligations. Over Perf_Fq the moduli formula is Spd(E)/phi^Z; Spd(breve E)/phi^Z is its separately proved Perf_k presentation for k = algebraic closure of F_q, not an unqualified replacement. Do not erase the characteristic-p integral untilt accepted by the supplier. In the matching mixed-characteristic p-typical specialization, reuse or construct canonical comparison isomorphisms to the already defined Mathlib BDeRhamPlus and BDeRham carriers (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean at 082e2d3). The latter is a localization at images of generators of the theta kernel; its existence as a definition does not prove principality, the theta extension, the DVR property or the required relative topological comparisons. Preserve those theorem obligations. These absolute carriers are zero when p = 0 in the input and do not replace the integral characteristic-p period rings.
RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts.reason: The integral degree-one closed-image argument must precede the integral degree-d construction; it cannot depend back on this whole generic-untilt stage. Completion is constructed once for the invertible divisor ideal, while its generic de Rham interpretation and base-field conversion are new comparisons here.

RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3.keeps: The direct rank-one Frobenius descent defining O(n) for integral n, its pi normalization, tensor, dual, divisor-section and transition-function API, and the eigenvalue normalization H^0(O(n)) = H^0(Y,O)^{phi = pi^n}. Keep the graded section algebra P, Proj(P), and the analytic-to-schematic map as a mathematical target. The unconditional chart construction first gives a map only on U = union of the nonvanishing loci of all positive-degree global sections. A map on all X_S requires a separately proved U = X_S covering lemma. Do not claim that quasicompactness alone proves this covering, or that O_Proj(P)(1) is automatically invertible with the asserted pullback for an arbitrary graded P. The location and proof of the covering/twist hypotheses remain the blocking RF3/VB2:ampleness boundary identified by REV-RS-20; none of these targets is deleted. Use VB1 as the sole owner of the arbitrary-rank exact tensor isocrystal-to-bundle functor and its general/rational-slope comparisons. The early rank-one descent here must not import the completed VB1 stage.
RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3.reason: The inherited isocrystal-line-bundles-and-sign node also constructs the full exact tensor functor, duplicating the explicit VB1 target. Separate its rank-one prefix (retained here) from the arbitrary-rank construction (VB1), and prove their agreement there. Preserve all existing IDs as references until the orchestrator transports the split proof payloads. The inherited graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map node extracts a global morphism and tautological-line statements without the requisite covering/generation input. FS II.2.7 is stated under generation and vanishing hypotheses; its local formula alone is not a no-hypothesis global construction. Adding VB2:ampleness back as a whole-stage prerequisite would create a cycle. This review does not approve that unresolved boundary.

Prove the Tannakian transfer of RF4:vector-bundles gluing, effectivity, independence of a faithful representation, change of structure group, base change and divisor compatibility. Actual loop/Grassmannian quotient and bounded-moduli constructions remain later GS0:loop-geometry applications of this theorem, not prerequisites of its proof.
